endpoints.summary: Lists prescriptions. Branches on req.user.userType: PHYSICIAN sees every prescription they authored (all statuses); anyone else (PATIENT/RECEPTIONIST/STAFF) sees only prescriptions whose visit.patientUserId is their own user id AND whose status is CONFIRMED/SENT/DISPENSED. Optional ?visitId filter. Physician results are enriched with a patientName field via a batched User lookup.
endpoints.auth: router.use(authCheck) (JWT Bearer, payload {id,email,role,userType,displayName,organizationId}) -> cacheMiddleware(15). In-handler gate: userType === 'PHYSICIAN' selects the physician branch (scoped to their own physicianProfile.id); every other userType falls into the patient branch scoped by visit.patientUserId === req.user.id. No auditLog. Global app-level rate limiter on /api (100 req/min/IP).
endpoints.responseShape:
JSON ARRAY (never null; [] when empty). PHYSICIAN branch element:
{
  "id": "uuid",
  "visitId": "uuid",
  "physicianId": "uuid",
  "subprofileId": "uuid" | null,
  "status": "DRAFT"|"SIGNED"|"CONFIRMED"|"SENT"|"DISPENSED",
  "medications": <raw Json column, echoed verbatim; normally an array of {drugName,dosage,frequency,duration,instructions} but may carry extra keys such as stoppedAt (ISO string) and stoppedByPatient (bool) added by the stop-medication route; can legally be any JSON value including {} or null>,
  "notes": "string" | null,
  "signedAt": "2026-09-03T10:15:30.123Z" | null,
  "sentToPatientAt": "ISO-8601 with ms + Z" | null,
  "pdfUrl": "string" | null,
  "refillRequestedAt": "ISO-8601" | null,
  "refillStatus": "string" | null,          // free-text column, values used elsewhere: PENDING|APPROVED|DENIED
  "refillNotes": "string" | null,
  "createdAt": "ISO-8601",
  "updatedAt": "ISO-8601",
  "deletedAt": "ISO-8601" | null,
  "visit": {
    "id": "uuid",
    "chiefComplaint": "string" | null,
    "visitDate": "ISO-8601",
    "patientUserId": "uuid",              // always present, non-null column
    "clinic": { "name": "string" }         // never null (clinicId is required on Visit)
  },
  "physician": {
    "specialty": "string",                 // non-null column
    "user": { "displayName": "string" }
  },
  "subprofile": { "name": "string", "relation": "SELF"|"SPOUSE"|"CHILD"|"PARENT"|"SIBLING"|"OTHER" } | null,
  "patientName": "string"                  // KEY IS ABSENT (not null) when the User row is missing
}

NON-PHYSICIAN branch element: byte-identical to the above MINUS the patientName key entirely (the enrichment block only runs for userType==='PHYSICIAN').

Ordering: createdAt DESC.
errorCases: 401 {"error":"No token provided"} when Authorization header is absent or does not start with 'Bearer '
401 {"error":"Invalid token"} when jwt.verify throws (bad signature, expired)
200 [] (NOT an error, and it IS cached for 15s) when userType==='PHYSICIAN' but no physicianProfile row exists for req.user.id
500 {"error":"Failed to list prescriptions"} on any thrown error, incl. Prisma rejecting a repeated ?visitId=a&visitId=b (Express parses it as an array)
429 {"error":"Too many requests, please try again later"} from the app-level /api limiter
requestQuery: visitId?: string — applied as an exact equality filter (where.visitId). No validation, no uuid check. If repeated in the query string Express yields an array and Prisma throws -> 500.
crossModelReads: PhysicianProfile (findUnique by userId, physician branch only)
User (findMany id IN patientIds, select id+displayName — physician branch only, skipped entirely when patientIds is empty)
sideEffects: Populates the in-memory response cache under key `route:<userId>:/api/prescriptions[?visitId=...]` for 15 seconds. Nothing in this router ever invalidates that cache.
quirks: patientName is set to `patientMap[...] || undefined`. JSON.stringify DROPS undefined values, so the key is COMPLETELY ABSENT from the object when the patient User row is missing — a .NET port must omit the property, not emit null or "".
patientName is added ONLY on the physician branch. The patient branch response has no patientName key at all.

There is NO deletedAt filter. Soft-deleted prescriptions (deletedAt != null) are returned, and deletedAt itself is exposed in the payload. Same for the joined visit — soft-deleted visits still resolve.

The physician branch applies NO status filter, so DRAFT prescriptions are visible to the physician. The patient branch filter is status IN ('CONFIRMED','SENT','DISPENSED') — note SIGNED is EXCLUDED even though POST / creates prescriptions with status 'SIGNED'. A freshly created prescription is therefore invisible to the patient until /sign (->CONFIRMED) or /send (->SENT) runs.

The branch key is userType, not the presence of a physicianProfile. A RECEPTIONIST or STAFF user is treated as a patient and will see prescriptions only if visit.patientUserId happens to equal their own user id — in practice an empty array.
A PHYSICIAN with no physicianProfile gets 200 [] (early return) rather than 403/404 — and that empty array is written into the 15s cache.

The cache key includes req.originalUrl, so /api/prescriptions and /api/prescriptions?visitId=x are cached separately. Cache is per-user so there is no cross-tenant leak, but a POST/PUT in this router never invalidates it: a client that creates then immediately re-lists can see stale data for up to 15s.
Cached hits are replayed through res.json(cached) with status 200 — the cached body is the JS object, so re-serialization is identical (undefined patientName stays dropped).

medications is a Prisma Json column echoed verbatim — the server does no shaping, so any extra keys the client originally POSTed are still there. In .NET this must be a raw JSON passthrough, not a typed DTO.
physician.specialty is a required (non-null) column so it is always a string, but physician.user.displayName is also always present — neither can be null here.
visit.clinic can never be null (clinicId is required on Visit), so the client's optional chaining on it is defensive only.
subprofile IS nullable (subprofileId is optional) — emit JSON null, not an empty object.

All DateTime fields serialize as JS Date -> ISO-8601 UTC with milliseconds and trailing Z (e.g. "2026-09-03T10:15:30.123Z"). visitDate/createdAt/updatedAt are non-null; signedAt/sentToPatientAt/refillRequestedAt/deletedAt are nullable.

Serialization key order follows Prisma's model field order then the include order: scalars (id, visitId, physicianId, subprofileId, status, medications, notes, signedAt, sentToPatientAt, pdfUrl, refillRequestedAt, refillStatus, refillNotes, createdAt, updatedAt, deletedAt) then visit, physician, subprofile, then patientName last (it comes from the object spread).
The N+1-avoidance batch de-dupes patient ids with a Set and filters falsy ids, but visit.patientUserId is a required column so the filter is a no-op.

endpoints.summary: Three prescription counts for the physician dashboard badge. Registered AFTER GET '/' and POST '/' but BEFORE GET '/:id' (L190), so it is not shadowed by the :id route.
endpoints.auth: router.use(authCheck) -> cacheMiddleware(30). No userType check at all — scoped purely by the caller's physicianProfile. Anyone without a physicianProfile (any patient) gets the all-zero object, not a 403.
errorCases: 401 {"error":"No token provided"} — missing/non-Bearer Authorization header
401 {"error":"Invalid token"} — jwt.verify failure
200 {"signed":0,"sent":0,"total":0} when the caller has no physicianProfile (early return, NOT an error, and it IS cached for 30s)
500 {"error":"Failed to get prescription summary"} on a thrown error
429 {"error":"Too many requests, please try again later"} from the app-level /api limiter
sideEffects: Writes the response into the 30s in-memory route cache.
quirks: The key is called "signed" but the count covers status IN ('CONFIRMED','SIGNED') — TWO statuses. A .NET port that counts only SIGNED will under-report, and since POST / creates as SIGNED while PUT /:id/sign writes CONFIRMED, both states legitimately land in this bucket.
signed + sent does NOT equal total. total counts every status including DRAFT and DISPENSED, and DISPENSED/DRAFT rows appear in neither signed nor sent.
NO deletedAt filter — soft-deleted prescriptions are counted in all three numbers.
No physicianProfile -> 200 with all zeros, cached for 30s. A patient calling this endpoint therefore gets a well-formed body, never an authorization error.

The three counts run in Promise.all, i.e. three separate COUNT queries with no shared snapshot/transaction — under concurrent writes the numbers can be mutually inconsistent (e.g. total lower than signed+sent).
The 30s TTL is longer than GET /'s 15s, so the dashboard badge and the list can visibly disagree after a status change.
Values are JSON numbers (Prisma count returns a JS number). Emit as int, not string.

endpoints.summary: Returns a complete, self-contained, print-ready HTML document for the prescription (NOT a real PDF, NOT JSON). Resolves the display name for the patient with a three-tier fallback, then hands everything to generateRxPDFHtml in server/src/services/pdfService.js. Declared at L874, well after GET '/:id' at L190, but the two-segment path means no route shadowing occurs.
endpoints.auth: router.use(authCheck) only. In-handler ownership gate AFTER the query: isPhysician = (physicianProfile exists for req.user.id) && prescription.physicianId === thatProfile.id; isPatient = prescription.visit.patientUserId === req.user.id. 403 unless one is true. No auditLog, no cacheMiddleware, no aiUsageCheck.
endpoints.responseShape:
NOT JSON. Content-Type: text/html; charset=utf-8 (the handler sets 'text/html' and Express's res.send appends '; charset=utf-8'). Express also adds ETag and Content-Length, and the global compression() middleware will gzip it when the client sends Accept-Encoding. Body is the literal string returned by generateRxPDFHtml: Rx {RXNUM} — {escaped physician.name}
[ only when clinic.logo is truthy]

{clinic.name || 'Clinic'}

{[clinic.address, clinic.city].filter(Boolean).join(', ')}

[

Tel: {clinic.phone}

only when phone is truthy]

Dr. {physician.user.displayName}

{physician.specialty || ''}

[

License: {licenseNumber}

only when truthy]
℞
Patient: {patientDisplayName}
Date: {rxDate}
Rx #: {rxNumber}
per medication, in array order:
#MedicationDosageFrequencyDuration
{i+1} {drugName}[
{instructions}
only when instructions truthy]		 {dosage || '—'}{frequency || '—'}{duration || '—'}
[
Notes: {prescription.notes}
only when notes is truthy]
Dr. {physician.name}
Electronically signed via Tebrazi · {rxDate}
Generated by Tebrazi — Digital Healthcare Platform  |  tebrazi.com
Derived values a port must reproduce exactly: rxNumber = prescription.id.slice(0,8).toUpperCase() // first 8 chars of the uuid, upper-cased, hyphen included if present rxDate = new Date(prescription.signedAt || prescription.createdAt).toLocaleDateString('en-GB', {day:'2-digit', month:'short', year:'numeric'}) // e.g. "03 Sep 2026" — Node full-ICU en-GB, day-month-year, no comma patientDisplayName: 1) if prescription.subprofile -> `${subprofile.name} (${subprofile.relation})` with the RAW ENUM, e.g. "Ahmed (CHILD)"; 2) else if visit.clinicPatient?.name -> that name; 3) else User.displayName for visit.patientUserId; 4) else the literal 'Patient'.
errorCases: 401 {"error":"No token provided"} — missing/non-Bearer header (JSON, application/json)
401 {"error":"Invalid token"} — jwt.verify failure
404 {"error":"Prescription not found"} when no row has that id (JSON, not HTML)
403 {"error":"Access denied"} when the caller is neither the authoring physician nor visit.patientUserId (JSON, not HTML)
500 {"error":"Failed to generate PDF"} on any thrown error
429 {"error":"Too many requests, please try again later"} from the app-level /api limiter
crossModelReads: PhysicianProfile (findUnique by userId, for the access check)
User (findUnique by visit.patientUserId, select displayName — ONLY reached when there is no subprofile AND no clinicPatient.name)
Clinic (nested select on visit: name, address, city, phone, logo)
externalDeps: server/src/services/pdfService.js -> generateRxPDFHtml (pure string builder, no I/O, no headless browser)
compression() app middleware gzips the HTML body
quirks: This endpoint is named /pdf but emits text/html — no PDF bytes, no application/pdf, no Content-Disposition. The client fetches it with axios responseType:'text' and document.write()s it into a new window (client/src/pages/PrescriptionsPage.jsx handleDownloadPDF, client/src/components/PrescriptionPanel.jsx). A .NET port MUST keep returning HTML, not generate a real PDF.
SUCCESS is HTML but every ERROR is JSON. Content-Type flips per branch because res.setHeader('Content-Type','text/html') runs only on the happy path, after all the checks.
Final success Content-Type is 'text/html; charset=utf-8' — Express's res.send appends the charset to the header the handler set. Emitting bare 'text/html' would not match.

The prescription is fetched BEFORE the authorization check, so an unauthorized caller still triggers the full joined query (timing/side-channel only, but the query order matters if you port it as a single guarded statement).
NO deletedAt filter — a soft-deleted prescription still renders a full PDF.

The subprofile branch WINS over clinicPatient and over the platform User. When a subprofile exists the patient name always reads "Name (RELATION)" with the raw uppercase enum (SELF/SPOUSE/CHILD/PARENT/SIBLING/OTHER) — it is never localized or prettified.
patientDisplayName is initialized to 'Patient' and the final else-branch also falls back to 'Patient' when the User row is missing, so an anonymous "Patient" is a real, reachable output.

rxDate uses signedAt WITH createdAt fallback. For a DRAFT (signedAt null) the printed date is the creation date, and the signature block claims "Electronically signed via Tebrazi · {that date}" even for an unsigned prescription.

rxDate is produced by JS toLocaleDateString('en-GB') and depends on the process's ICU data and default timezone — the date shown is the SERVER-LOCAL calendar day of the UTC instant. A .NET port must format with en-GB "dd MMM yyyy" against the server's local timezone to match.
toLocaleDateString('en-GB', month:'short') yields "03 Sep 2026" (no comma, zero-padded day, three-letter month, no trailing period).

rxNumber is a naive id.slice(0,8) — for a standard uuid that is the first hex group (8 chars, no hyphen), but the code makes no assumption, so if ids ever get shorter/other-shaped it just takes whatever is there.

escapeHtml() escapes & < > " ' (apostrophe as ') and returns '' for ANY falsy input including 0 and false. The `escapeHtml(x) || '—'` idiom therefore renders an em dash (U+2014) for empty/missing dosage, frequency and duration — not an empty cell.
`escapeHtml(med.drugName) || ''` for the drug name has NO em-dash fallback: a medication with no drugName renders .
clinic.logo is injected into src="..." after escapeHtml — but the global request-body sanitizer does not touch DB-stored values, so whatever URL is in the DB goes straight into the img tag.

`clinic: prescription.visit.clinic || { name: 'Clinic' }` is dead defensive code — Visit.clinicId is required, so clinic is never null. The `escapeHtml(clinic.name) || 'Clinic'` fallback is likewise unreachable in practice (Clinic.name is non-null).
medications: `Array.isArray(...) ? ... : []` — a non-array Json value yields an EMPTY <tbody> (the table header still renders). Never null, never an error.

The address

renders as an empty

element when both clinic.address and clinic.city are null — the tag is always emitted.
The HTML contains an inline onclick="window.print()" button and emoji (🖨, ℞) — must be byte-preserved and served as UTF-8.

Every template hole is interpolated from a template literal, so leading/trailing whitespace and newlines inside the markup are part of the response body. Byte-identical output requires reproducing the template's exact indentation, including the trailing newline pattern of the medicationRows .map(...).join('') (each row starts with a newline and is indented 4 spaces).
The medications array order is the stored order — no sorting, no filtering of patient-stopped meds (a med with stoppedAt still prints).

endpoints.summary: Physician creates a prescription against one of their own visits. AUTO-SIGNS at creation: status is written as 'SIGNED' and signedAt as now(), so the /sign endpoint is not required. subprofileId is inherited from the visit, not from the request body.
endpoints.auth: router.use(authCheck) -> auditLog('CREATE','prescription') -> handler. In-handler gate: the caller MUST have a physicianProfile (else 400), and the target visit must satisfy {id: visitId, physicianId: myProfile.id} (else 403). NO userType check — a non-PHYSICIAN userType that somehow owns a physicianProfile would pass.
endpoints.responseShape:
{
  "id": "uuid",
  "visitId": "uuid",
  "physicianId": "uuid",
  "subprofileId": "uuid" | null,        // copied from visit.subprofileId, NOT from the request
  "status": "SIGNED",                   // always literally SIGNED on create
  "medications": <the request array echoed back verbatim from the Json column, extra keys and all>,
  "notes": "string" | null,
  "signedAt": "ISO-8601",               // always set on create, never null here
  "sentToPatientAt": null,
  "pdfUrl": null,
  "refillRequestedAt": null,
  "refillStatus": null,
  "refillNotes": null,
  "createdAt": "ISO-8601",
  "updatedAt": "ISO-8601",
  "deletedAt": null,
  "visit": { "chiefComplaint": "string" | null, "visitDate": "ISO-8601" }   // ONLY these two keys — NO id
}
errorCases: 400 {"error":"visitId and at least one medication are required"} when visitId is falsy, OR medications is falsy, OR medications is not an Array, OR medications.length === 0
400 {"error":"Physician profile required"} when no physicianProfile row exists for req.user.id — note this is 400, NOT 403
403 {"error":"Visit not found or not yours"} when no visit matches {id: visitId, physicianId: myProfile.id} — a nonexistent visit id also yields 403, never 404
401 {"error":"No token provided"} / 401 {"error":"Invalid token"} from authCheck
500 {"error":"Failed to create prescription"} on any thrown error (e.g. an FK violation)
413 (Express raw error) when the JSON body exceeds the 10mb express.json limit
429 {"error":"Too many requests, please try again later"} from the app-level /api limiter
requestBody: visitId: string — REQUIRED (truthiness check only, no uuid validation)

medications: array — REQUIRED, must be a non-empty Array. Element shape is NOT validated at all: the array is stored raw into the Json column. The documented element shape is {drugName, dosage, frequency, duration, instructions} but any JSON is accepted, including primitives, nulls, or objects with none of those keys.
notes?: string — optional; stored as `notes || null` so '' , 0 and false all become NULL
(any other body keys are silently ignored — subprofileId, status, signedAt from the client are NOT honored)
dbWrites: prescriptions — INSERT (NOT in a transaction). Columns set: visitId, physicianId, subprofileId, medications, notes, status='SIGNED', signedAt=now(); the rest take schema defaults (status default DRAFT is overridden, id uuid, createdAt/updatedAt now(), pdfUrl/sentToPatientAt/refill*/deletedAt null).
activity_logs — INSERT via the auditLog middleware, fire-and-forget (.catch(()=>{})), NOT in a transaction, and it runs on the res.json interception so it can complete after the response is flushed.
externalDeps: Global body sanitizer in server/src/index.js (see quirks)
sideEffects: activity_logs row: {userId: req.user.id, action:'CREATE', resource:'prescription', resourceId: <new prescription id>, metadata:{method:'POST', path:'/api/prescriptions'}, ipAddress: req.ip, userAgent: first 256 chars of the UA header}. Only written when res.statusCode < 400, so the 400/403 branches log nothing.
No notification is sent, no reminder is created, and NO route cache is invalidated — GET / and GET /summary keep serving pre-create data for up to 15s / 30s.
quirks: Named 'create' but it AUTO-SIGNS: status='SIGNED' and signedAt=new Date(). A port that respects the schema default (DRAFT) breaks the whole downstream flow.
The created row's status 'SIGNED' is NOT in the patient list filter of GET / ('CONFIRMED','SENT','DISPENSED'), so the patient cannot see a just-created prescription until /sign or /send runs.

The 201 response's nested visit object has ONLY chiefComplaint and visitDate — no id, no patientUserId, no clinic. This is a DIFFERENT visit shape from GET / and GET /:id. The response also has no physician and no subprofile object at all.
Missing physician profile returns 400, not 403 — but a foreign/nonexistent visit returns 403, not 404. Both status codes are counter-intuitive and must be copied exactly.
The visit lookup uses findFirst with no deletedAt filter, so a SOFT-DELETED visit still accepts new prescriptions.
subprofileId is silently taken from visit.subprofileId. If the visit has none (a clinicPatient-chart visit), subprofileId is null and the PDF route will then fall back to clinicPatient.name.
notes uses `notes || null`, so an empty-string notes field is persisted as SQL NULL, not ''.

medications is stored with zero server-side normalization — no trimming, no drugName requirement per element, no dedup. `[null]` and `[{}]` and `[1,2,3]` are all accepted (length 1, Array.isArray true).

GLOBAL BODY SANITIZER: server/src/index.js recursively rewrites every string in req.body before this handler sees it — it strips <script>/<iframe>/<style>/etc. tags and on*= handlers, deletes the substrings 'javascript:', 'data:' and 'vbscript:' (case-insensitive), strips 'expression(' and rewrites 'url(' to 'url\('. So a drug name or instruction containing e.g. 'data:' or 'url(' is MUTATED before storage. A .NET port must reproduce this sanitizer to keep stored values identical.
The auditLog middleware picks resourceId as `req.params?.id || data?.id` — on POST / there is no :id param so it uses the new prescription's id from the response body.
No transaction wraps the insert plus the audit row; the audit insert is fire-and-forget and its failure is swallowed silently.
Response key order is Prisma model order for scalars, then `visit` last.

endpoints.summary: Sets the prescription's status to CONFIRMED (not SIGNED) and stamps signedAt=now(). Ownership-checked against the caller's physicianProfile. No status precondition whatsoever.
endpoints.auth: router.use(authCheck) only. In-handler gate: physicianProfile must exist for req.user.id AND prescription.physicianId must equal that profile's id, else 403. No auditLog, no userType check, no cacheMiddleware.
endpoints.responseShape:
{
  "id": "uuid",
  "visitId": "uuid",
  "physicianId": "uuid",
  "subprofileId": "uuid" | null,
  "status": "CONFIRMED",              // ALWAYS the literal CONFIRMED, never SIGNED
  "medications": <raw Json, unchanged>,
  "notes": "string" | null,
  "signedAt": "ISO-8601",             // freshly set to now(), never null in this response
  "sentToPatientAt": "ISO-8601" | null,
  "pdfUrl": "string" | null,
  "refillRequestedAt": "ISO-8601" | null,
  "refillStatus": "string" | null,
  "refillNotes": "string" | null,
  "createdAt": "ISO-8601",
  "updatedAt": "ISO-8601",            // bumped by @updatedAt
  "deletedAt": "ISO-8601" | null,
  "message": "Prescription signed"    // extra key appended by the object spread, LAST
}
Flat — no visit, no physician, no subprofile objects (the update call has no include).
errorCases: 404 {"error":"Prescription not found"} when no row has that id
403 {"error":"Not your prescription"} when the caller has no physicianProfile OR prescription.physicianId !== myProfile.id (both conditions collapse into this one message)
401 {"error":"No token provided"} / 401 {"error":"Invalid token"} from authCheck
500 {"error":"Failed to sign prescription"} on any thrown error
429 {"error":"Too many requests, please try again later"} from the app-level /api limiter
requestBody: NONE. The body is read but never used — the client sends no body at all (api.put(`/prescriptions/${id}/sign`)).
dbWrites: prescriptions — UPDATE SET status='CONFIRMED', signedAt=now(), updatedAt=now() WHERE id=:id. NOT in a transaction.
sideEffects: None — no notification, no reminder, no audit row, no cache invalidation. GET / and GET /summary keep serving the pre-sign status for up to 15s/30s.
quirks: THE BIG ONE: the endpoint called /sign writes status 'CONFIRMED', while POST / writes 'SIGNED'. The PrescriptionStatus enum has both. A port that writes SIGNED here silently breaks the patient list filter and the /summary counts are unaffected only because 'signed' counts BOTH.

NO status precondition. Signing a prescription that is already SENT or DISPENSED succeeds and REGRESSES its status back to CONFIRMED, while leaving sentToPatientAt populated — producing a row that is CONFIRMED but has a sentToPatientAt timestamp.
signedAt is overwritten on every call, so re-signing loses the original signature timestamp.
No deletedAt filter — a soft-deleted prescription can be signed.

The 403 message 'Not your prescription' is emitted both for 'caller is not a physician at all' and for 'prescription belongs to another physician'. There is no distinct 'physician profile required' message here (unlike POST /, which uses 400 'Physician profile required').
The prescription row is fetched with a bare findUnique and then updated in a separate statement — a classic read-then-write with no optimistic concurrency, so two concurrent signs both succeed.

The `message` key is appended by `{...updated, message: ...}` so it serializes LAST, after deletedAt. The client does not read it, but byte-identical JSON requires the key and its exact string 'Prescription signed'.
There is a separate PUT '/:id' route at L242 that DOES guard on status==='SENT'; /:id/sign has no such guard. Route order is fine — '/:id' cannot shadow '/:id/sign' because of the extra path segment.
No auditLog middleware on this route, unlike POST /.

endpoints.summary: Sets status to SENT + sentToPatientAt=now(), notifies the patient (in-app + email + push), then AUTO-CREATES daily-recurring MEDICATION reminders for every medication that has both a drugName and a frequency — first deleting any existing ACTIVE MEDICATION reminders whose title contains that drug name. Both the notification and the reminder blocks are individually try/catch-swallowed, so the response never reflects their failure.
endpoints.auth: router.use(authCheck) only. In-handler gate: physicianProfile must exist for req.user.id AND prescription.physicianId === that profile's id, else 403. No auditLog, no userType check.
endpoints.responseShape:
{
  "id": "uuid",
  "visitId": "uuid",
  "physicianId": "uuid",
  "subprofileId": "uuid" | null,
  "status": "SENT",                        // always the literal SENT
  "medications": <raw Json, UNCHANGED — send never rewrites medications>,
  "notes": "string" | null,
  "signedAt": "ISO-8601" | null,           // NOT touched here; can still be null if the row was a DRAFT
  "sentToPatientAt": "ISO-8601",           // freshly set, never null in this response
  "pdfUrl": "string" | null,
  "refillRequestedAt": "ISO-8601" | null,
  "refillStatus": "string" | null,
  "refillNotes": "string" | null,
  "createdAt": "ISO-8601",
  "updatedAt": "ISO-8601",
  "deletedAt": "ISO-8601" | null,
  "message": "Prescription sent to patient"   // LAST key, from the spread
}
Flat — no include, so no visit/physician/subprofile. NOTHING about the notification or the created reminders appears in the response (no count, no ids).
errorCases: 404 {"error":"Prescription not found"} when no row has that id
403 {"error":"Not your prescription"} when the caller has no physicianProfile OR the prescription belongs to another physician
401 {"error":"No token provided"} / 401 {"error":"Invalid token"} from authCheck

500 {"error":"Failed to send prescription"} — reachable ONLY from the findUnique / physicianProfile lookup / the status UPDATE itself; every notification and reminder failure is caught and logged, never surfaced
429 {"error":"Too many requests, please try again later"} from the app-level /api limiter
requestBody: NONE. Body is never read. The client calls api.put(`/prescriptions/${id}/send`) with no payload.
dbWrites: prescriptions — UPDATE SET status='SENT', sentToPatientAt=now(), updatedAt=now() WHERE id=:id. NOT in a transaction, and it happens BEFORE all the side effects.
notifications — INSERT (type 'PRESCRIPTION_SENT'), best-effort in its own try/catch
reminders — DELETE MANY per medication: WHERE userId=<patient> AND type='MEDICATION' AND title CONTAINS <drugName> AND status='ACTIVE'
reminders — INSERT one row per dose time per medication (1-12 rows per med), best-effort
notifications — a SECOND INSERT (type 'MEDICATION_REMINDER_SET') only when remindersCreated > 0
device_tokens — possible DELETE MANY of dead tokens inside pushService, per notification
crossModelReads: Visit (findUnique by prescription.visitId, select patientUserId) — queried TWICE, once in the notification block and again in the reminder block
User (findUnique by req.user.id, select displayName — the sending doctor's name for the notification text)
User (findUnique inside createNotification, select email+displayName, only because sendEmail:true)
externalDeps: server/src/services/notificationService.js -> createNotification (lazily required INSIDE the handler, twice)
server/src/services/emailService.js -> sendEmail (reached because sendEmail:true on the first notification)
sideEffects: Notification #1 (only when visit.patientUserId is truthy): {userId: <patient>, type:'PRESCRIPTION_SENT', title:'New Prescription Available', message:`Dr. ${docUser?.displayName || 'Your doctor'} has sent you a new prescription. View it in your Prescriptions page.`, data:{prescriptionId: <:id from the URL>}, sendEmail:true}

Email to the patient (subject = the notification title, html = `

{title}

{message}

`, text = `{title}\n\n{message}`), fired inside createNotification because sendEmail:true; failure is console.error'd only
Push notification to every DeviceToken of the patient: {title, body: message, data: {prescriptionId}} — always attempted, errors swallowed

Reminder purge: for EACH medication, deleteMany over reminders WHERE userId=<patient> AND type='MEDICATION' AND title CONTAINS drugName AND status='ACTIVE' — this is a SUBSTRING match, so it wipes that drug's ACTIVE reminders originating from ANY other prescription too

Reminder creation: for each dose time i (0-based) of each medication -> {userId:<patient>, createdById: req.user.id (the physician's USER id), title:`💊 ${drugName}${doseLabel}`, description:`${dosage ? dosage + ' — ' : ''}Take at ${timeStr}`, type:'MEDICATION', remindAt: <local Date>, recurrence:'DAILY', prescriptionId: <:id>, notes: JSON.stringify({drugName, dosage, frequency, doseNumber: i+1, totalDoses: dosesPerDay, intervalHours})}

Notification #2 (only when remindersCreated > 0): {userId:<patient>, type:'MEDICATION_REMINDER_SET', title:'Medication Reminders Set', message:`${n} medication reminder${n > 1 ? 's have' : ' has'} been automatically created from your new prescription.`, data:{prescriptionId}, sendEmail:false} — push is still attempted
logger.info({prescriptionId, remindersCreated}, '[Prescriptions] Auto-created medication reminders') — only inside the `patientUserId && medications.length > 0` branch
quirks: NO status precondition — the comment 'Auto-sign is now done at creation — no DRAFT block needed' documents the removal of the guard. You can /send a DRAFT (status becomes SENT while signedAt stays NULL), and you can re-send a DISPENSED prescription, REGRESSING its status from DISPENSED back to SENT.

Every re-send re-runs the full side-effect chain: another patient notification + email + push, another reminder purge, and a fresh set of reminder rows. There is no idempotency key and no check on sentToPatientAt.
signedAt is NOT set here — only status and sentToPatientAt change.
'Dr. ' is hardcoded in front of docUser.displayName, so a displayName already containing a title renders as 'Dr. Dr. Ahmed ...'.
The notification's data.prescriptionId uses the raw `id` from req.params, not updated.id — identical in practice, but note it is the URL string.
Visit is queried TWICE for the same patientUserId (once per side-effect block) — two round trips for one value.
The reminder block reads `prescription.medications` from the PRE-update snapshot, not from `updated`. Same value in practice since send does not touch medications.
A medication is skipped when `!med.frequency || !med.drugName` — so meds with an empty-string frequency produce no reminders and no purge, silently.

parseFrequency: 'every N h' -> round(24/N); '<n> times a day|daily|/day' -> n; 'three times|thrice|tid' -> 3; 'twice|two times|bid|2x' -> 2; 'four times|qid|4x' -> 4; 'once|one time|od|1x' -> 1; otherwise 1. Result is CLAMPED to 1..12 and intervalHours = Math.round(24/dosesPerDay). Regex order matters: the 'twice|...|b.i.d' branch is tested BEFORE 'four times|q.i.d', and 'three times|t.i.d' before both. The 'od' pattern is `o\.?d` which also matches inside unrelated words.

getDefaultDoseTimes: 1->['08:00']; 2->['08:00','20:00']; 3->['08:00','14:00','20:00']; 4->['08:00','12:00','18:00','22:00']; 5+ -> evenly spaced from 08:00 with wraparound modulo 24h (so a 5-dose schedule wraps past midnight and reminder times are NOT in ascending order).

Dose times are computed with `new Date()` then setHours(h,m,0,0) in the SERVER's local timezone, not the patient's. If that local instant is already past, the date is bumped +1 day — so remindAt is 'today or tomorrow at the server's local h:m'.
doseLabel is '' when dosesPerDay === 1, otherwise ` (Dose ${i+1}/${dosesPerDay})` — note the leading space, and 1-based numbering.

timeStr = doseTime.toLocaleTimeString('en-US', {hour:'2-digit', minute:'2-digit', hour12:true}) — yields e.g. '08:00 AM' (zero-padded 12-hour with a non-breaking-space-or-space before AM/PM depending on the ICU version; this is embedded in the reminder description, not in the HTTP response).

The reminder title starts with the 💊 emoji plus a space: `💊 Metformin (Dose 1/2)`. The purge matches on `contains: drugName`, a case-SENSITIVE substring on Postgres, so 'Metformin' will not purge a reminder titled with 'metformin', and a short drug name that is a substring of another drug's name will purge that other drug's reminders too.
The purge only targets status='ACTIVE' reminders, so COMPLETED/CANCELLED ones survive and can accumulate.

Reminder.createdById is the PHYSICIAN's user id while Reminder.userId is the patient's — and Reminder.patientUserId is left NULL even though the schema comment says it is 'set when physician creates for a patient'.

Reminder.notes is a JSON STRING (JSON.stringify output), not a Json column — it must be persisted as text with exactly those keys in that order: drugName, dosage, frequency, doseNumber, totalDoses, intervalHours.

`dosage` defaults to '' (`med.dosage || ''`), and the description then omits the ' — ' separator entirely when dosage is empty: 'Take at 08:00 AM' vs '500mg — Take at 08:00 AM' (em dash U+2014 surrounded by spaces).

Reminder creation is sequential and un-transactioned (an await inside a for inside a for). A mid-loop failure leaves the earlier reminders created, the purge already applied, the prescription already SENT, and returns 200 with no indication of the partial state.

remindersCreated is only computed inside `if (patientUserId && medications.length > 0)`, so the '[Prescriptions] Auto-created medication reminders' log line and Notification #2 never fire for an empty medications array.
No deletedAt filter — a soft-deleted prescription can be sent, notified about, and generate reminders.

The response carries NO information about the reminders or notification, so a .NET port can fail these side effects entirely and still produce byte-identical JSON — but the patient's reminders and inbox would silently differ.
Both notificationService requires are lazy `require(...)` calls inside the handler (twice), presumably to dodge a circular import.
No auditLog middleware on this route.

endpoints.summary: Marks the prescription DISPENSED and optionally decrements clinic inventory for a caller-supplied list of {itemId, quantity}. Each item gets an atomic decrement paired with an inventoryTransaction row in a $transaction; if the resulting stock is negative the decrement is rolled back (but the transaction row is NOT) and the item is omitted from the response.
endpoints.auth: router.use(authCheck) only. In-handler gate: physicianProfile must exist for req.user.id AND prescription.physicianId === that profile's id, else 403. NO ownership/clinic check on the inventory items at all. No auditLog, no userType check.
endpoints.responseShape:
{
  "id": "uuid",
  "visitId": "uuid",
  "physicianId": "uuid",
  "subprofileId": "uuid" | null,
  "status": "DISPENSED",                  // always the literal DISPENSED
  "medications": <raw Json, unchanged>,
  "notes": "string" | null,
  "signedAt": "ISO-8601" | null,
  "sentToPatientAt": "ISO-8601" | null,
  "pdfUrl": "string" | null,
  "refillRequestedAt": "ISO-8601" | null,
  "refillStatus": "string" | null,
  "refillNotes": "string" | null,
  "createdAt": "ISO-8601",
  "updatedAt": "ISO-8601",
  "deletedAt": "ISO-8601" | null,
  "message": "Prescription dispensed",
  "inventoryDeducted": [                  // ALWAYS an array, [] when no items were supplied or all were skipped. NEVER null, never absent.
    {
      "itemId": "uuid",                   // echoed from the request, not re-read
      "name": "string",                   // InventoryItem.name from the PRE-decrement read
      "quantity": <int>,                  // parseInt(request quantity) — the POSITIVE number, even though the transaction row stores -qty
      "newStock": <int>                   // the item's currentStock AFTER the atomic decrement
    }
  ]
}
The two extra keys are appended by the spread, so `message` then `inventoryDeducted` serialize LAST, in that order. Flat otherwise — the update has no include.
errorCases: 404 {"error":"Prescription not found"} when no row has that id
403 {"error":"Not your prescription"} when the caller has no physicianProfile OR the prescription belongs to another physician
401 {"error":"No token provided"} / 401 {"error":"Invalid token"} from authCheck

500 {"error":"Failed to dispense prescription"} on any thrown error — INCLUDING a Prisma failure inside the inventory loop (e.g. a non-numeric quantity producing NaN, or a concurrent FK problem). The prescription has ALREADY been set to DISPENSED by then, so the client sees a 500 for a mutation that partially succeeded.
429 {"error":"Too many requests, please try again later"} from the app-level /api limiter
requestBody: inventoryItems?: array of { itemId: string, quantity: number|string } — entirely OPTIONAL. Only processed when Array.isArray(inventoryItems) && length > 0; any non-array value (object, string, null, undefined) is silently ignored and inventoryDeducted comes back []. The client in PrescriptionsPage.jsx sends NO body at all.
dbWrites: prescriptions — UPDATE SET status='DISPENSED', updatedAt=now() WHERE id=:id. NOT in a transaction, and it runs BEFORE any inventory work.
inventory_items — UPDATE currentStock = currentStock - qty (atomic decrement), inside prisma.$transaction, one transaction PER item

inventory_transactions — INSERT inside the SAME $transaction: {itemId, type:'DISPENSED', quantity: -qty, previousStock: <stale pre-read item.currentStock>, newStock: Math.max(0, item.currentStock - qty), prescriptionId: <:id>, notes:'Dispensed via prescription', performedById: req.user.id}
inventory_items — a COMPENSATING UPDATE currentStock = currentStock + qty (increment), OUTSIDE any transaction, when the post-decrement currentStock is negative
crossModelReads: InventoryItem (findUnique by itemId, one per requested item — full row read before the decrement)
sideEffects: One inventory_transactions row of type DISPENSED per attempted item — INCLUDING items whose decrement is subsequently rolled back for insufficient stock.
Stock levels change on inventory_items. No notification, no audit row, no cache invalidation, no reminder work.
quirks: NO status precondition. You can dispense a DRAFT or an already-DISPENSED prescription; each call re-runs the inventory deduction, so double-submitting double-deducts stock.

NO clinic/tenant scoping on itemId. `prisma.inventoryItem.findUnique({where:{id: itemId}})` accepts ANY inventory item id in the whole database — a physician can decrement another clinic's stock. A faithful port must reproduce this (or the client's behavior changes), but flag it.

ROLLBACK LEAK: when the post-decrement currentStock < 0, only the inventory_items row is incremented back — the inventory_transactions row created in the same $transaction is left in place. The DB ends up with an orphan DISPENSED row (negative quantity) for a deduction that never happened, and the item silently does NOT appear in inventoryDeducted. The client gets 200 with no hint that the item was skipped.
The compensating increment is a bare update OUTSIDE a transaction, so a crash between the two leaves stock permanently short.

previousStock and the transaction's newStock come from the STALE pre-read `item.currentStock`, while the item's real new value comes from the atomic decrement. Under concurrency the transaction row's newStock does NOT match the item's actual currentStock, and the response's `newStock` (from updatedItem) can differ from the row's newStock.
The transaction row's newStock is clamped with Math.max(0, ...) but the item's currentStock is NOT clamped — the item can genuinely go negative before the rollback check reads it.
`if (!itemId || !quantity) continue;` uses truthiness: quantity 0, '', null, undefined and false all skip the item silently. Skipped items produce no transaction row and no response entry.

quantity goes through parseInt(quantity) with no radix and no validation: '3.9' -> 3; '5abc' -> 5; 'abc' -> NaN, which reaches Prisma's decrement and THROWS -> 500 with the prescription already DISPENSED and any earlier items already deducted.

A NEGATIVE quantity (e.g. -5) passes the truthiness check and becomes `decrement: -5`, i.e. it INCREASES stock. The rollback check (< 0) does not fire, and the response reports {quantity: -5, newStock: <increased>} while the transaction row stores quantity: +5 (because it writes -qty).
`if (!item || !item.isActive) continue;` — a missing or soft-inactive item is silently skipped, no error, no response entry.
The $transaction destructures `const [updatedItem, tx] = ...` and `tx` is never used (dead variable).
One $transaction per item, not one for the whole batch, so a mid-batch failure leaves earlier items deducted.

inventoryDeducted is initialized to `let deducted = []` and always emitted — even when no inventoryItems were sent. It is an empty ARRAY, never null and never an omitted key. Elements are pushed in request order (minus skipped items).
The `name` in each element is InventoryItem.name from before the decrement — a response key that comes from a DIFFERENT model than everything else in the payload.
The response's element key is `itemId` (echoed from the request), not `id` — it does NOT match InventoryItem's primary-key field name.
The prescription status UPDATE is not part of any inventory transaction: a total inventory failure still leaves the prescription DISPENSED.
No deletedAt filter — a soft-deleted prescription can be dispensed.
`message` ('Prescription dispensed') and `inventoryDeducted` are appended after all the model scalars via the object spread, in that exact order.
No auditLog middleware, even though this mutates inventory.
